answer: The finality of attestations only counts when the attestator is established, so a fresh cluster of aliases cannot push any transaction to finality until it has spent many epochs proving honesty. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a saffron as the anchor of the cost.
